Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, $d,n\ge1$, and let $S=S(d,n)$ be the
$q$-Schur algebra over $F$ with Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$
([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Let $M$ be a finite
dimensional right $S$-module all of whose composition factors lie in a single
block $B$ of $S$
([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]),
and let integers $a_{\lambda}$, $\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$, satisfy
$$[M]=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}]$$
in the Grothendieck group $G_0(S\text{-mod})$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]). Then
$W^{\lambda}$ lies in $B$ whenever $a_{\lambda}\ne0$. In particular no nonzero
virtual combination of Weyl classes all of whose terms lie outside $B$ can
equal the class of a module in $B$.

**Given:** A field $F$, $q\in F^{\times}$, $d,n\ge1$, the algebra $S=S(d,n)$
with Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}$, $\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$, a finite
dimensional right $S$-module $M$ whose composition factors all lie in one
block $B$, and integers $a_{\lambda}$ with
$[M]=\sum_{\lambda}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}]$ in $G_0(S\text{-mod})$
([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]],
[[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]).

[F2] Each Weyl module $W^{\lambda}$ has simple head $L^{\lambda}$, with
$[W^{\lambda}:L^{\lambda}]=1$ and $[W^{\lambda}:L^{\mu}]\neq0\Rightarrow
\lambda\unrhd\mu$; in particular every composition factor of $W^{\lambda}$ lies
in the block containing the simple module $L^{\lambda}$, and this is the block
of $W^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [F1]).

current_incoming_paragraphs: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^\times$, $\ell=e(F,q)$, and $n\ge r\ge1$; at the empty lower-rank boundary put $S(0,0)=H(0)=F$ with its identity functor. Use the left-module version of the q-Schur algebra $S(n,r)$ and its exact Schur functor $f_{n,r}:V\mapsto eV$ with left adjoint $h_{n,r}:X\mapsto S(n,r)e\otimes_{eS(n,r)e}X$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]). Right-module suppliers are converted to left modules through their star anti-involutions. All Specht and simple labels below are **Murphy labels**: $f(W^\mu)=S_{\mathrm M}^\mu$ and $f(L_n(\mu))=D_{\mathrm M}^\mu$, the latter nonzero exactly when $\mu$ is $\ell$-restricted ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]).

[F1] The permutation-summand realization is $S(n,r)=\operatorname{End}_{H(r)}(\bigoplus_\alpha M^\alpha)$, with weight projections $1_\alpha$. The regular summand for a composition with exactly $r$ entries equal to $1$ is $M^\alpha=H(r)$. The standard corner is $\omega=(1^r,0^{n-r})$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]).

[F4] Every Schur simple $L(\mu)$ is its nonzero cell-form quotient, so the descended symmetric associative form makes $L(\mu)^\circ\cong L(\mu)$ under Schur star. The normalized maps are $\varphi_{ST}(x_\nu h)=m_{ST}h$, with $m_{ST}\in x_\mu H\cap Hx_\nu$ and $m_{TS}=m_{ST}^*$; Schur star is $\varphi_{ST}^*=\varphi_{TS}$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). The standard coefficient trace satisfies $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ and $\tau(T_u^*T_v)=\delta_{uv}q^{\ell(u)}$; its complete generator-block proof is the actual standalone trace construction of [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]. The following proof establishes the restricted-socle conclusion locally over the original field; no quantum-hyperalgebra square-root or unproved classical-specialization premise is used.

current_incoming_paragraphs: Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]), let $d\ge n$, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl modules of $S_F(d,n)$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Then for partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts, $W^{\lambda}_F$ and $W^{\mu}_F$ lie in the same block of $S_F(d,n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently the blocks of $S_F(d,n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|\le n$ and $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ every partition is its own core and every Weyl module is its own block, the algebra being semisimple.)

Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, $e=e(F,q)$ and $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). For
$\lambda\vdash n$ and $e$-regular $\mu\vdash n$ let
$$d_{\lambda\mu}:=[S^{\lambda}:D^{\mu}],$$
the multiplicity of $D^{\mu}$ in a composition series of the Specht module
$S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]],
[[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]). Then
$$d_{\mu\mu}=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_{\lambda\mu}\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu\unrhd\lambda,$$
where $\unrhd$ is the dominance order on partitions
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]): a simple factor $D^{\mu}$ of
$S^{\lambda}$ can occur only if the $e$-regular label $\mu$ dominates
$\lambda$. Equivalently the decomposition matrix $(d_{\lambda\mu})$ is
unitriangular along dominance. This constrains but does not compute the
entries: no off-diagonal decomposition number is determined by cellularity.

**Given:** A field $F$, $q\in F^{\times}$, $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$ with Specht modules $S^{\lambda}$ and simple quotients $D^{\mu}$ in the signed conjugate normalization ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]), together with the dominance order on partitions of $n$ ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]).

[F1] ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) $S^{\lambda}=(S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$ and $D^{\mu}=(D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$ for the conjugate partitions, where $S^{\nu}_{\mathrm M}$ is the Murphy cell module and $\theta$ is the involutive automorphism $\theta(T_i)=-qT_i^{-1}$; pullback along $\theta$ is exact and preserves submodules, quotients, composition multiplicities and simplicity.

Take $R=\mathbb C[\hat q]_{(1+\hat q)}$, the prime element $\pi=1+\hat q$ (so that $F=\mathbb C$ and $q:=\hat q+\pi R$ specialises to $-1$, giving $e=2$), and $\lambda=(3,2)$, $n=5$. Evaluating the q-Schaper virtual sums ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula, thm-q-schur-weyl-weight-space-gram-determinant-hook-product, thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules, lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form, lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening, thm-nonzero-cell-heads-classify-the-simple-modules-of-a-cellular-algebra]]) with the hook valuations $
u_\pi([2]_{\hat q})=
u_\pi([4]_{\hat q})=1$, $
u_\pi([3]_{\hat q})=
u_\pi([1]_{\hat q})=0$ gives, in the source's normalisation, $$\sum_{i>0} igl[W^{(3,2)}_F(i) igr]= igl[W^{(3,1^2)}_F igr]+ igl[W^{(2^2,1)}_F igr]- igl[W^{(1^5)}_F igr],\qquad \sum_{i>0} igl[S^{(3,2)}_F(i) igr]=2 igl[D^{(2^2,1)}_{\mathrm{M}} igr].$$ Further Jantzen calculations give $W^{(1^5)}_F=L^{(1^5)}_F$, $W^{(2^2,1)}_F=L^{(2^2,1)}_F$ and $W^{(3,1^2)}_F\sim L^{(3,1^2)}_F+L^{(2^2,1)}_F+L^{(1^5)}_F$, so at the level of the sum formula alone one gets $d_{(3,2),(3,1^2)}=1$ and only the bound $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}\in\{1,2\}$. The extra dimension/filtration argument on the Specht side gives $S^{(3,2)}_{\mathrm{M}}\cong D^{(2^2,1)}_{\mathrm{M}}$ (both sides have dimension $5$), whence $d_{(3,2),(2^2,1)}=1$: the virtual sum alone did not determine the entry. Translated to the Dipper-James convention of this page by conjugating and applying the same $	heta$ pullback to both modules ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]), this reads $S^{(2,2,1)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong D^{(3,2)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$, while the partition $(2,2,1)$ is not $2$-regular, so its own labelled cell-form quotient vanishes, $D^{(2,2,1)}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=0$. The computed entry is consistent with the dominance bound $d_{\lambda\mu}
e0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$ of [[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]].

1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row
   symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of
   $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra
   $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy
   basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht
   module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is
   the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention:
   $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with
   the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the
   specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}$ whose
   radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$
   ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when
   $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when
   $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$
   ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in
   characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is
   $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$
   ([[thm-specht-radical-quotient-is-nonzero-exactly-for-p-regular-partitions]]),
   and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has
   $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$. This matches the group-side
   classification
   [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the
   conjugate-sign dictionary
   [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]].
   In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht
   modules are irreducible.

[F1] ([[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]]) The Dipper-James ordinary Specht module with its polytabloid basis and standard form is identified with the signed conjugate Murphy cell module of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] by a base-change compatible isomorphism whose Laurent unit form factor is $q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_{\lambda})}$, equal to $1$ at $q=1$ over every field; hence at $q=1$ the ordinary module and the standard form agree on the specialization, including on zero-form quotients.

$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

current_incoming_paragraphs: The hypothesis $e>n$ in [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]] cannot be dropped. Take $F=\mathbb C$, $q=-1$ (so $e=e(\mathbb C,-1)=2$, [[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), $n=3$ and $\lambda=(2,1)$. The two distinct standard tableaux $s=\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\3\end{smallmatrix}$ and $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ have contents $\operatorname{content}_s(1),\operatorname{content}_s(2),\operatorname{content}_s(3)=0,1,-1$ and $\operatorname{content}_t(1),\operatorname{content}_t(2),\operatorname{content}_t(3)=0,-1,1$, and the extended quantum-integer identity gives $[1]_{-1}=1=[-1]_{-1}$, since $[-1]_{-1}=-(-1)^{-1}[1]_{-1}=1$. Hence $$([\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}=(0,1,1)=([\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}\quad(q=-1):$$ the q-content sequences collide although $s\ne t$, so the separation conclusion of the theorem fails. The difference of the two putative separating eigenvalues at $k=2$ is $[-1]_{-1}-[1]_{-1}=0$. Thus interpolation cannot distinguish the two tableaux: a formula that excludes equal values may still define a polynomial, but it is not a separating projector for these two labels. The attempted generator formula has axial distance $\rho=2$ and $[\rho]_{-1}=0$. In fact $L_2$ has a nontrivial Jordan block on this cell, so this cell has no simultaneous JM-eigenbasis. This explicit example shows that the uniform separation hypothesis $e>n$ cannot be dropped; it does not claim that every individual cell at every parameter with $e\le n$ lacks a seminormal basis.
